Implementation Plan

I found the cause. In `_shell_segments_with_operators` (`.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:272-279`), the only check on the character just before the raw digits is that it isn't a backslash. shlex turns `''2`, `""2` and `''12` into the bare token `2` or `12`, and the raw text right before `>` is still the digits, so the guard drops the token. Bash, however, passes that token to git as a refspec. A separate `gh_api_write_guard.py` has similar digit-dropping, but it is a different hook with different semantics, so I'm leaving it out of scope. Writing the plan now.

## Implementation plan: empty-quoted numeric refspec bypasses the merge-status guard

Refs #3576 (tracking; no auto-close keyword).

**Planning ref:** `claude/hopeful-fermat-9pb74t` @ `7c3c5c376bb0b732b8d071ef760431b87b0f80fc`. Integration branch metadata matches (no mismatch).

### Automation / wiring (§20.E)
- **Only modifies existing code.** No new script, workflow, scheduler entry, supervisor or DB operation.
- **Entry point:** unchanged. The hook runs as a Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook through `.claude/settings.json` and its `workflow-templates/.claude/settings.json` mirror. CI runs `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py`.
- **Long-running supervisor:** none needed.
- **DB gate:** not applicable.
- **`docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry:** none (no new script).

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends _shell_segments_with_operators
Scope-mode justification: The bug sits in one condition of the existing lexer helper `_shell_segments_with_operators`. It decides whether a numeric word in front of a redirect is a file descriptor. Today it confirms only that the raw text right before the redirect equals the token and is not preceded by a backslash. It does not check that this text is the whole raw word. The full fix is to require a shell word boundary before the raw digits. That is about the same size as a narrower "also reject quote characters" patch, and it also covers `\2`, `'1'2` and any other way a quote or escape can make bare digits that bash treats as an argument. No new dependency or interface is added. The parallel digit-dropping in `.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py` (`_shell_segments`, line ~451) is a different hook with a different contract and is not part of this finding, so scope stays on the merge-status guard and its template mirror.

### 1. Files likely to change
- `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`: the redirect branch of `_shell_segments_with_operators` (lines ~263-283).
- `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`: byte-identical copy of the same edit. `test_template_copies_are_identical` enforces this.
- `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py`: new regression cases.
- `changelog.d/<issue-number>-merge-guard-empty-quote-fd.md`: new fragment (CLAUDE.md §20 / `<!-- changelog: fixed -->`). Use this issue's number in the file name.

### 2. Functions to change
`_shell_segments_with_operators(command)`, in the branch where `token` is a redirect operator (`<`, `>`, `>>`, `>&`, `&>`, etc.):

Current logic (lines 272-279): pop `segment[-1]` when all of these hold:
- the token does not start with `&`;
- `segment[-1]` is ASCII digits;
- the token is adjacent to the redirect (`previous_end == token_end - len(token)`);
- `command[raw_start:previous_end-1] == segment[-1]`;
- the character at `raw_start - 1` is not `\`.

New logic: keep the first four conditions. Replace the backslash test with a **word-boundary test**: `raw_start == 0` or `command[raw_start - 1]` is one of the lexer's word delimiters, which are the whitespace set `" \t\r"` plus `_SHELL_PUNCTUATION_CHARS` (`";&|\n<>"`). Only then is the entire raw word unquoted ASCII digits directly against the redirect, which is the only case where bash reads it as an FD.
- `''2>`, `""2>`, `''12>`: preceded by `'` or `"`, so the token is kept as a refspec.
- `\2>`, `\12>`: preceded by `\`, so kept, as today. The new boundary test covers these cases, which makes the old explicit backslash check redundant.
- `'1'2>`: the raw slice still differs from the token, so it is kept, as today.
- `2>`, `x;2>`, a word at the start of a segment, `\t2>`: delimiter before, so the token is popped, as today.

Use a module-level `frozenset` constant for the delimiter set. Name it `_SHELL_WORD_DELIMITERS`, after grepping that the name is unused in the module (§10). Build it from `" \t\r"` and `_SHELL_PUNCTUATION_CHARS` so it cannot drift from the lexer configuration. Update the inline comment to say: "pop only when the whole raw word is unquoted ASCII digits adjacent to the redirect; any quote/escape in the word keeps it as an argument".

**Fail-closed rule:** whenever the raw word cannot be shown to be exactly the unquoted digits, the token stays in the argument list. Keeping it is both the safe choice and the correct bash meaning, because bash passes it to git as a refspec. `_push_targets` then checks branch `2`, or asks for confirmation when `_branch_ref` returns `None`. It never falls back silently to the current branch.

### 3. Data structures affected
None. `_GitInvocation`, `_GuardTarget` and the return shape of `_shell_segments_with_operators` (`list[tuple[str, list[str]]]`) are unchanged.

### 4. API / interface changes
None. Hook stdin/stdout contract, exit codes, env vars and log text are unchanged.

## Decisions

### D1 — Word-boundary check instead of a quote-character blocklist
- **Chosen:** Pop the numeric token only when the character before its raw span is a lexer word delimiter (whitespace or `_SHELL_PUNCTUATION_CHARS`) or the start of the command.
- **Alternatives considered:**
  - (a) Add `'` and `"` to the existing `!= "\\"` test.
  - (b) Rebuild per-token quote provenance with a custom tokenizer.
  - (c) Never pop numeric tokens.
- **Why:**
  - (a) is a blocklist that misses future quote or escape forms (for example `$''`).
  - (b) is a much larger rewrite of a security-sensitive lexer.
  - (c) breaks the documented `git push origin 2>/dev/null` behavior, where bash really does use an FD, and the existing tests that pin it.
  - A delimiter allowlist matches bash's rule that an FD prefix must be a whole unquoted word, and fails closed on everything else.

### D2 — Keep the token instead of requesting confirmation on ambiguity
- **Chosen:** Leave an unconfirmed numeric word in the argument list.
- **Alternatives considered:** Mark the invocation uncertain and request confirmation.
- **Why:** In every ambiguous case the issue covers, bash really does pass the word to git as an argument. Keeping it makes the guard check the branch git will push. Non-literal shapes already go through `_branch_ref` → `None`, which asks for confirmation.

## Security considerations
- **Trust boundary:** the model-authored Bash `command` string reaching the PreToolUse hook. It is untrusted input, and the hook is the only automated barrier against pushing new commits onto a branch whose PR already merged (CLAUDE.md, merge-status rule near line 878).
- **Authorization:** no new endpoint or surface. The change narrows when the hook may drop a word from the push arguments.
- **Input validation:** the decision now depends on the raw command bytes around the token, not only on the token shlex produced. That closes the gap between how shlex and bash treat empty quotes.
- **Abuse cases closed:**
  - From `main`: `git push origin ''2>/dev/null` and `git push origin ""2>/dev/null` used to skip the PR lookup for branch `2`.
  - The same holds for multi-digit names: `''12>`, `""123>>`.
  - The same holds for `''2&>` / `""2>&1`-style shapes, where `&` follows the digits.
- **No regressions to FD stripping:** genuine FD redirects (`2>/dev/null`, `2>&1`) still drop the FD and keep checking the real destination branch, as `test_adjacent_fd_redirect_does_not_create_numeric_refspec` already requires.
- **No secrets or logging changes.**

### 5. Risks and edge cases
- **`previous_end` arithmetic:** the existing calculation assumes shlex read exactly one lookahead character (the first redirect character). The new check reuses the same `raw_start`, so this assumption does not change. Add a test where the digits are the first word of a segment after `;`, so that `raw_start - 1` landing on a punctuation character is covered.
- **`raw_start == 0`:** a command that starts with `2>x` has no git invocation, so this is harmless. Keep the guard against a negative index.
- **Backslash-newline before the digits** (`origin \` + newline + `2>/dev/null`): shlex yields a token that is not ASCII digits, so it is not popped. `_branch_ref` then returns `None`, which asks for confirmation (fail-closed). This is unchanged and needs no work, but note it in the PR body.
- **Template parity:** both hook copies must be edited byte-identically, or `test_template_copies_are_identical` fails. Edit one copy and copy it over.
- **Out of scope (noted, not changed):** `.claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py::_shell_segments` drops any digit token before a redirect without an adjacency check. That hook guards `gh api` writes, not branch pushes. File it separately if needed. Do not change it here.

### 6. Testing considerations
In `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py`:
- Extend the `test_numeric_push_refspec_before_redirect_is_checked` parametrization, where the repo creates branch `<refspec>`, checks out `main`, and expects a block with `lookups == [refspec]`. Add:
  - `("2", "git push origin ''2>/dev/null")`
  - `("2", 'git push origin ""2>/dev/null')`
  - `("12", "git push origin ''12>/tmp/out")`
  - `("2", "git push origin ''2&>/tmp/out")`
  - `("123", 'git push origin ""123>>/dev/null')`
- Add a unit test on `guard._shell_segments_with_operators` / `_guarded_git_invocations`. It asserts that `git push origin ''2>/dev/null` keeps `"2"` in `arguments` (`["origin", "2"]`), while `git push origin 2>/dev/null` still yields `["origin"]`.
